::: {#exr-miller-taylor-poly-nonzero}
#### Taylor expansion of a polynomial at a nonzero point

Adapted from @problifesavercalc, Question 1.1.17.

Find the first three terms (up to degree 2) of the Taylor series for

$$f(x) = x^8 + x^4 + 3$$

at $x_0 = 1$.
:::

::: {#sol-miller-taylor-poly-nonzero}
Evaluate $f$ and its first two derivatives at $x_0 = 1$:

$$\ba
f(1) &= 1^8 + 1^4 + 3 \\
&= 5
\\
f'(1) &= 8(1)^7 + 4(1)^3 \\
&= 12
\\
f''(1) &= 56(1)^6 + 12(1)^2 \\
&= 68
\ea$$

The degree-2 Taylor polynomial is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
P_2(x)
&= f(1) + f'(1)(x - 1) + \frac{f''(1)}{2!}(x - 1)^2 \\
&= 5 + 12(x - 1) + 34(x - 1)^2
\end{aligned}
$$
:::
